None of them appears in a source apportionment, because none of them is a source. **Nitrogen sensitivity is a derived property of a damaged system**, and the accounting treats it as a constant.\n\n## 8. What this does and does not establish\n\n**It does not establish that agriculture is off the hook.** Multiplying unknown fractions yields an unknown, not a small one. Agriculture is plausibly still the largest single nitrogen contributor, the load is real, and reductions have documented local benefits.\n\n**It does not establish that nitrogen policy failed.** Necessary and insufficient are different findings, and the record is consistent with the second.\n\n**It does establish that the number is not what it is presented as.** \"69.6% of nitrogen\" is a residual of models over one term of an open account. \"70% of fedtemøg\" is that residual multiplied by four coefficients that have never been computed. The first is a defensible piece of bookkeeping. The second is not a measurement of anything.\n\n**And it establishes an asymmetry in what gets counted.** Every term that would shift blame away from a countable source — deposition, regeneration, groundwater, legacy, temperature, state — is precisely a term with no row. That may be coincidence of what is easy to measure. It is worth noticing that the easy measurements and the politically actionable ones are the same set.\n\n### The practical consequence\n\nIf nitrogen were the whole binding constraint, this would be a solved problem in principle: catch crops, wetlands, treatment upgrades, and extractive aquaculture are all available, and we have already deployed enough of them to halve the load. Either the remaining reduction needed is far larger than anything currently proposed, or nitrogen is not the whole binding constraint.\n\nBoth readings sit in the same record. **That thirty-five years of data cannot distinguish them is the strongest single argument that the accounting is measuring the wrong thing.**\n\n## 9. What would separate the readings\n\n| To test | Do this |\n|---|---|\n| Whether the extremes track load at all | Regress annual iltsvind extent on flow-normalised load, wind-work over the stratified season, and bottom-water temperature anomaly. All three series exist and are published. Nobody has published the regression. |\n| Whether state-dependence is real | The same regression with an interaction term, or simply: does a given load produce more hypoxia now than in 1990, holding weather constant? Answerable from existing DCE series. |\n| Whether the denominator can be closed | Two of the ten empty rows are tractable with standard methods — submarine groundwater discharge via radon/radium tracers, internal regeneration via benthic flux chambers. Both are routine elsewhere. |\n| Whether the potency term matters | Weight existing load figures by season and receiving-water stratification. Even a crude weighting beats the current implicit weight of 1.0 everywhere. |\n| Whether fedtemøg has the season everyone assumes | Fixed coastal cameras, monthly index, year-round. The cheapest item on this list by an order of magnitude, and the only claim here that is currently unfalsifiable in either direction. |\n\nNone of these needs new instruments. Four of the five need no new data at all — only that two published series be plotted against each other.\n\n---\n\n*Sources for the load and outcome series, with URLs, are in `data/manual/monitoring.json` under `load_trend_vs_outcome`. And therefore no denominator, and no percentages — until the empty rows are filled.\n\nNote the scale of what the apportionment omits. Atmospheric deposition to Danish marine waters is 45–90 kt N/yr, comparable to the entire land-based waterborne term, and appears in none of the published shares.\n\n## 2. The numbers are not estimators of what they are named\n\nEach line of the published apportionment, relabelled by what actually produced it:\n\n| Called | Actually is |\n|---|---|\n| **Agriculture, 69.6%** | **Residual.** (grab-sampled load over 49% of the area + model output over 51%) minus modelled point sources minus modelled natural background, with retention modelled at ±6-27 percentage points. |\n| **Natural background, 22.1%** | Model output — and the subtrahend that determines the residual above. |\n| **Treatment plants, 4.8%** | **Reported effluent monitoring.** Flow-metered, routinely sampled. The best-measured line in the table. |\n| **Aquaculture and marine farms, 1.5%** | Reported, feed-balance based. |\n| **Separate stormwater, 0.7%** | Modelled volume × a concentration from a **1990** measurement programme. |\n| **Rain-dependent overflow, 0.6%** | Modelled volume (30-135% stated uncertainty) × an assumed concentration, quality-controlled **against that same assumed concentration**. |\n| **Industry, 0.5%** | Reported. |\n| **Scattered dwellings, 0.2%** | Modelled from dwelling counts × assumed per-capita loads. |\n\nTwo of these are measurements. The rest are models, and the largest is a residual of models.\n\n### The validation is circular\n\nReported nitrogen divided by reported volume must fall within **10–12 mg/l** for combined sewers and **1.8–2.2 mg/l** for separate ones. Outside that, *\"kontaktes den dataansvarlige med henblik på at få rettet eventuelle fejl\"* — the data owner is contacted to correct the error.\n\nThe check tests conformity to the assumed concentration, not accuracy. A genuinely high measured first-flush concentration would be flagged as a mistake. **The assumed concentration cannot be falsified by data collected under it.**\n\n### And the estimator can return impossible values\n\nIn dry years such as 1996 and 2005 the calculated cultivation contribution comes out NEGATIVE - described in the literature as a meaningless result caused by the uncertainty in the assessment. A residual whose error can exceed its own signal is published to one decimal place with no error bar.\n\nUnderneath it: **240 stream stations** covering **49%** of the country, the other **51%** modelled. Load is grab samples plus linear interpolation, and in all three streams of the 2018 validation study that method **always underestimated** — annual deviations -0.9% to -7.7%, monthly deviations reaching +98%. Retention, the largest single term, carries **±6–27 percentage points**.\n\n### Overflow is modelled, and the deciding variable is not collected\n\n| Knowledge level | Method | Stated uncertainty |\n|---|---|---:|\n| 0 | PULS calculation | — |\n| 1 | Simple mass balance | 135% |\n| 2 | Uncalibrated 1D hydrodynamic model (Mike Urban) | 100% |\n| 3 | Calibrated Mike Urban | 55% |\n| 4 | Software sensor / CFD | 45% |\n| 5 | Measurement-based | 30% |\n\nPULS records 'antal overløb' - the number of overflows. It records no flow rate, no peak and no threshold crossing, so a high-flow event that scours accumulated basin sediment cannot be distinguished from a small dilute one.\n\nThat matters because sediment resuspension is a **threshold** in flow, not a frequency of events. Below the critical shear stress the deposit stays in the basin; above it, the accumulated sludge leaves — and the hazardous-substances programme reports the highest median metal concentrations precisely in basin sludge. Multiplying an annual volume by an average concentration cannot represent that, and the resulting error is one-directional and largest in the wettest years.\n\n## 3. Nitrogen mass is the wrong currency\n\nOxygen depletion is the damage. Nitrogen is one route to it. Converting everything to oxygen demand — Redfield stoichiometry, which is chemistry rather than judgement:\n\n| Pathway | Oxygen demand |\n|---|---:|\n| Remineralisation of algal biomass | **19.70 g O₂ per g N** |\n| Remineralisation, via phosphorus | 142.6 g O₂ per g P |\n| **Nitrification of delivered ammonium** | **4.57 g O₂ per g N** |\n| **Sulphide oxidation** | **2.00 g O₂ per g S** |\n| Methane oxidation | 3.99 g O₂ per g CH₄ |\n| Direct BOD | 1.46 g O₂ per g BOD₅ |\n\nOnly the first line is modelled by the accounts. Three consequences:\n\n**Ammonium carries its own demand.** An ammonium-rich discharge — which is what a basin that has gone anaerobic produces — consumes 4.57 g O₂ per g N on arrival, with no algae, no light and no delay. That pathway is absent from a nitrogen→algae→decay model entirely.\n\n**Sulphate makes the debt effectively unbounded.** Seawater holds ~2700 mg/l sulphate = 901 mg/l as sulphur, against ~8 mg/l dissolved oxygen. Fully reduced and later re-oxidised that is 1799 mg/l of demand — **225× the oxygen in the water**. Reducing just 0.44% of the sulphate pool stores a debt equal to all of it. Once a basin goes anoxic the electron acceptor is effectively infinite, and every storm that mixes oxygen in spends it re-oxidising sulphide instead of restoring the water.\n\n**And the ratio matters, not just the total.** Diatoms need silicon roughly 1:1 with nitrogen. Fertiliser and sewage add N and P; neither adds silicon, which comes from rock weathering. Enrichment therefore raises N:Si, and when silicon runs out the community shifts from diatoms to flagellates and dinoflagellates. A composition change driven by a ratio, invisible to any nitrogen total.\n\nThere is no potency term anywhere in the accounting. A kilogram delivered in February into a mixed column counts identically to a kilogram delivered in July into a stratified fjord — though vertical mixing across a summer pycnocline is roughly four orders of magnitude weaker, which is what decides whether the nitrogen is used or flushed.\n\n## 4. What is not measured\n\n| What | Window | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| iltsvind DCE | Jul-Aug, Aug-Sep, Sep-Oct, Oct-Nov | set by mechanism (the stratified season) |\n| soft bottom fauna | 1 March - 31 May | set by programme design |\n| bathing water | bathing season, roughly June-September | set by human use **(circular)** |\n| fedtemoeg as a shore condition | no systematic national monitoring | set by when people are on beaches and complain **(circular)** |\n\nThe most consequential row is the second. **Soft-bottom fauna is sampled 1 March to 31 May** — after the winter, before the summer. The annual die-off is observed only in its aftermath, months later, once recolonisation has begun. So the event that decides which organisms are present to receive the next year's nitrogen is the one thing nobody watches.\n\nAnd any seasonal claim drawn from a seasonally-sampled record is circular unless the window was set by mechanism. Iltsvind's July–November window was; bathing water's June–September window was not.\n\n### Toxicants: eleven stations\n\nThe national typetal for hazardous substances in rain-dependent discharges — applied to all **19,665** discharge points — rest on **6 combined-sewer overflows and 5 separate stormwater outlets**, monitored 2000–2020.\n\nThe catchments were deliberately chosen to represent households and residential areas. The typetal cover only discharges *typetal cover only discharges 'uden forudgaaende rensning i form af fx filtrering eller sedimentation i regnvandsbassiner'*, and the report states they are limiting for *explicitly limiting for 'industriomraader og meget trafikerede veje'*.\n\nMeanwhile the same programme reports the highest median metal concentrations in sludge from basins. **The design excludes the worst cases, and says so.**\n\n| µg/l | Combined overflow | Separate stormwater | Max observed |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Zink | 170 | 130 | 400 |\n| Kobber | 16 | 9.0 | 50 |\n| Bly | 5.0 | 4.0 | 24 |\n| Chrom | 2.4 | 4.0 | 8.0 |\n| Nikkel | 2.7 | 4.0 | 9.0 |\n| Arsen | 0.8 | 1.3 | 4.0 |\n| Cadmium | 0.1 | 0.07 | 0.31 |\n| Kviksoelv | 0.05 | 0.03 | 0.3 |\n\nNote that chromium, nickel and arsenic are **higher in separated stormwater than in sewage overflow** — and nationally there is 195 million m³/yr of the former against 33 million m³/yr of the latter. Separating a sewer system solves the sewage overflow and delivers untreated road runoff instead.\n\n## 5. A worked case: Køge Bugt\n\nDCE's oxygen reports state, in both 2023 and 2025: *\"Køge Bugt og Faxe Bugt er der ikke registreret iltsvind i år\"* — **no oxygen depletion registered**, including in 2023, the worst iltsvind year in two decades.\n\nDCE's iltsvind is dissolved oxygen below 4 mg/l in bottom water, mapped in stratified basins. Køge Bugt is shallow and mixes readily, so it may never qualify while still having anoxic sediment, sulphate reduction and a putrefying shoreline. 'Not registered' is probably accurate and says nothing about whether the bay is dead.\n\n### Who can discharge sewage into the bay\n\n| Municipality | Separate outfalls | Combined overflows | % separated | Basin m³ |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| **København** | 116 | 19 | 86% | 42,750 |\n| **Hvidovre** | 18 | 22 | 45% | 19,858 |\n| **Tårnby** | 4 | 5 | 44% | 17,464 |\n| **Brøndby** | 18 | 1 | 95% | 0 |\n| Vallensbæk | 27 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Ishøj | 54 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Greve | 127 | 2 | 98% | 0 |\n| Solrød | 78 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Køge | 233 | 12 | 95% | 0 |\n| Stevns | 57 | 24 | 70% | 7,271 |\n\nVallensbæk, Ishøj and Solrød have **zero** combined-sewer overflows; Greve has two. The shoreline communities separated their systems and physically cannot discharge sewage into the bay in a storm.\n\n**92% of the bay's basin storage** (80,072 of 87,343 m³) sits in København, Hvidovre and Tårnby, along with 47 of 85 combined overflows. The bay opens southeast, so the discharge enters at the northern end and the whole shoreline is downstream of it. **The municipality that built the storage is not the one that smells it.**\n\n### Treatment capacity discharging to the bay\n\n| Plant | PE | Municipality |\n|---|---:|---|\n| Spildevandscenter Avedøre | 400,000 | Hvidovre |\n| Køge-Egnens Renseanlæg I/S | 100,000 | Køge |\n| Tårnby | 71,000 | Tårnby |\n| Mosede | 60,000 | Greve |\n| Solrød | 24,500 | Solrød |\n| Strøby Ladeplads | 13,000 | Stevns |\n| ST.HEDDINGE | 12,000 | Stevns |\n\n## What this does and does not establish\n\n**It does not establish that urban discharge is the dominant national source.** Under every reconstruction attempted, including ones stacked generously in that direction, agriculture remained the largest nitrogen term. Load is grab samples plus linear interpolation, and in all three streams of the 2018 validation study that method **always underestimated** — annual deviations -0.9% to -7.7%, monthly deviations reaching +98%. Retention, the largest single term, carries **±6–27 percentage points**.\n\n### Overflow is modelled, and the deciding variable is not collected\n\n| Knowledge level | Method | Stated uncertainty |\n|---|---|---:|\n| 0 | PULS calculation | — |\n| 1 | Simple mass balance | 135% |\n| 2 | Uncalibrated 1D hydrodynamic model (Mike Urban) | 100% |\n| 3 | Calibrated Mike Urban | 55% |\n| 4 | Software sensor / CFD | 45% |\n| 5 | Measurement-based | 30% |\n\nPULS records 'antal overløb' - the number of overflows. It records no flow rate, no peak and no threshold crossing, so a high-flow event that scours accumulated basin sediment cannot be distinguished from a small dilute one.\n\nThat matters because sediment resuspension is a **threshold** in flow, not a frequency of events. Below the critical shear stress the deposit stays in the basin; above it, the accumulated sludge leaves — and the hazardous-substances programme reports the highest median metal concentrations precisely in basin sludge. Multiplying an annual volume by an average concentration cannot represent that, and the resulting error is one-directional and largest in the wettest years.\n\n## 3. Nitrogen mass is the wrong currency\n\nOxygen depletion is the damage. Nitrogen is one route to it. Converting everything to oxygen demand — Redfield stoichiometry, which is chemistry rather than judgement:\n\n| Pathway | Oxygen demand |\n|---|---:|\n| Remineralisation of algal biomass | **19.70 g O₂ per g N** |\n| Remineralisation, via phosphorus | 142.6 g O₂ per g P |\n| **Nitrification of delivered ammonium** | **4.57 g O₂ per g N** |\n| **Sulphide oxidation** | **2.00 g O₂ per g S** |\n| Methane oxidation | 3.99 g O₂ per g CH₄ |\n| Direct BOD | 1.46 g O₂ per g BOD₅ |\n\nOnly the first line is modelled by the accounts. Three consequences:\n\n**Ammonium carries its own demand.** An ammonium-rich discharge — which is what a basin that has gone anaerobic produces — consumes 4.57 g O₂ per g N on arrival, with no algae, no light and no delay. That pathway is absent from a nitrogen→algae→decay model entirely.\n\n**Sulphate makes the debt effectively unbounded.** Seawater holds ~2700 mg/l sulphate = 901 mg/l as sulphur, against ~8 mg/l dissolved oxygen. Fully reduced and later re-oxidised that is 1799 mg/l of demand — **225× the oxygen in the water**. Reducing just 0.44% of the sulphate pool stores a debt equal to all of it. Once a basin goes anoxic the electron acceptor is effectively infinite, and every storm that mixes oxygen in spends it re-oxidising sulphide instead of restoring the water.\n\n**And the ratio matters, not just the total.** Diatoms need silicon roughly 1:1 with nitrogen. Fertiliser and sewage add N and P; neither adds silicon, which comes from rock weathering. Enrichment therefore raises N:Si, and when silicon runs out the community shifts from diatoms to flagellates and dinoflagellates. A composition change driven by a ratio, invisible to any nitrogen total.\n\nThere is no potency term anywhere in the accounting. A kilogram delivered in February into a mixed column counts identically to a kilogram delivered in July into a stratified fjord — though vertical mixing across a summer pycnocline is roughly four orders of magnitude weaker, which is what decides whether the nitrogen is used or flushed.\n\n## 4. What is not measured\n\n| What | Window | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| iltsvind DCE | Jul-Aug, Aug-Sep, Sep-Oct, Oct-Nov | set by mechanism (the stratified season) |\n| soft bottom fauna | 1 March - 31 May | set by programme design |\n| bathing water | bathing season, roughly June-September | set by human use **(circular)** |\n| fedtemoeg as a shore condition | no systematic national monitoring | set by when people are on beaches and complain **(circular)** |\n\nThe most consequential row is the second. **Soft-bottom fauna is sampled 1 March to 31 May** — after the winter, before the summer. The annual die-off is observed only in its aftermath, months later, once recolonisation has begun. So the event that decides which organisms are present to receive the next year's nitrogen is the one thing nobody watches.\n\nAnd any seasonal claim drawn from a seasonally-sampled record is circular unless the window was set by mechanism. Iltsvind's July–November window was; bathing water's June–September window was not.\n\n### Toxicants: eleven stations\n\nThe national typetal for hazardous substances in rain-dependent discharges — applied to all **19,665** discharge points — rest on **6 combined-sewer overflows and 5 separate stormwater outlets**, monitored 2000–2020.\n\nThe catchments were deliberately chosen to represent households and residential areas. The typetal cover only discharges *typetal cover only discharges 'uden forudgaaende rensning i form af fx filtrering eller sedimentation i regnvandsbassiner'*, and the report states they are limiting for *explicitly limiting for 'industriomraader og meget trafikerede veje'*.\n\nMeanwhile the same programme reports the highest median metal concentrations in sludge from basins. **The design excludes the worst cases, and says so.**\n\n| µg/l | Combined overflow | Separate stormwater | Max observed |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Zink | 170 | 130 | 400 |\n| Kobber | 16 | 9.0 | 50 |\n| Bly | 5.0 | 4.0 | 24 |\n| Chrom | 2.4 | 4.0 | 8.0 |\n| Nikkel | 2.7 | 4.0 | 9.0 |\n| Arsen | 0.8 | 1.3 | 4.0 |\n| Cadmium | 0.1 | 0.07 | 0.31 |\n| Kviksoelv | 0.05 | 0.03 | 0.3 |\n\nNote that chromium, nickel and arsenic are **higher in separated stormwater than in sewage overflow** — and nationally there is 195 million m³/yr of the former against 33 million m³/yr of the latter. Separating a sewer system solves the sewage overflow and delivers untreated road runoff instead.\n\n## 5. A worked case: Køge Bugt\n\nDCE's oxygen reports state, in both 2023 and 2025: *\"Køge Bugt og Faxe Bugt er der ikke registreret iltsvind i år\"* — **no oxygen depletion registered**, including in 2023, the worst iltsvind year in two decades.\n\nDCE's iltsvind is dissolved oxygen below 4 mg/l in bottom water, mapped in stratified basins. Køge Bugt is shallow and mixes readily, so it may never qualify while still having anoxic sediment, sulphate reduction and a putrefying shoreline. 'Not registered' is probably accurate and says nothing about whether the bay is dead.\n\n### Who can discharge sewage into the bay\n\n| Municipality | Separate outfalls | Combined overflows | % separated | Basin m³ |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| **København** | 116 | 19 | 86% | 42,750 |\n| **Hvidovre** | 18 | 22 | 45% | 19,858 |\n| **Tårnby** | 4 | 5 | 44% | 17,464 |\n| **Brøndby** | 18 | 1 | 95% | 0 |\n| Vallensbæk | 27 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Ishøj | 54 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Greve | 127 | 2 | 98% | 0 |\n| Solrød | 78 | 0 | 100% | 0 |\n| Køge | 233 | 12 | 95% | 0 |\n| Stevns | 57 | 24 | 70% | 7,271 |\n\nVallensbæk, Ishøj and Solrød have **zero** combined-sewer overflows; Greve has two. The shoreline communities separated their systems and physically cannot discharge sewage into the bay in a storm.\n\n**92% of the bay's basin storage** (80,072 of 87,343 m³) sits in København, Hvidovre and Tårnby, along with 47 of 85 combined overflows. The bay opens southeast, so the discharge enters at the northern end and the whole shoreline is downstream of it. **The municipality that built the storage is not the one that smells it.**\n\n### Treatment capacity discharging to the bay\n\n| Plant | PE | Municipality |\n|---|---:|---|\n| Spildevandscenter Avedøre | 400,000 | Hvidovre |\n| Køge-Egnens Renseanlæg I/S | 100,000 | Køge |\n| Tårnby | 71,000 | Tårnby |\n| Mosede | 60,000 | Greve |\n| Solrød | 24,500 | Solrød |\n| Strøby Ladeplads | 13,000 | Stevns |\n| ST.HEDDINGE | 12,000 | Stevns |\n\n## What this does and does not establish\n\n**It does not establish that urban discharge is the dominant national source.** Under every reconstruction attempted, including ones stacked generously in that direction, agriculture remained the largest nitrogen term. Stacking every identified bias in the overflow figures reaches roughly 10% of the land-based term — material, far above the published 0.6%, and still not the driver.\n\n**It does establish that the published percentage answers a different question than the one it is used for.** It answers: *of the nitrogen we observe arriving by stream from Danish land, how much do we attribute to farming after subtracting our models of everything else?* It is read as: *how much of Denmark's marine nitrogen problem is agriculture?*\n\nThose differ by a closed set, a potency term, and a state variable. The accounts contain none of the three.\n\n**Bounds marked as ours are ours.** Several ranges in section 1 are constructed here from the biases identified, not published figures. {"parentUuid":"d7f98524-f40a-4eca-9166-64ac87e2acea","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"8466ba53-c2d3-48d8-830a-8d25f83bea98","agentId":"a07c69a10b5af910f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KV72qsJ4PaVHqnzgmpd8Rx","type":"tool_result","content":"# The seabed, the wind, and what stays put\n\nGenerated by `scripts/seabed.py`. Wind from the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (1995-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 271,752 hourly records), coastline from OpenStreetMap, everything else computed.\n\n## Why this is computable without a current model\n\nIn a shallow bay the thing that lifts sediment off the bed is orbital motion under waves, and that follows from wind speed, direction, fetch and depth. Currents redistribute what the waves have already lifted — important, and not done here, because it needs data behind registration.\n\nThe chain: wind → fetch by direction (ray-cast to the OSM coastline) → fetch-limited wave height and period (Young & Verhagen 1996, shallow-water form) → bottom orbital velocity (linear wave theory) → bed shear stress (Swart friction factor) → compared against the critical stress for a living bed and a dead one.\n\n## Fetch: Køge Bugt is a southeast-facing funnel\n\n| Wind from | Fetch |\n|---|---:|\n| N | 6.5 km |\n| NE | 7.5 km |\n| E | 31.8 km |\n| SE | **120.0 km** |\n| S | 19.3 km |\n| SW | 17.5 km |\n| W | 9.5 km |\n| NW | 5.8 km |\n\nSoutheast runs to 120 km — the open Baltic approach — against under 20 km in almost every other direction. Southeast is also the **onshore** direction for the western shore. The bay's longest wave fetch and its stranding direction are the same.\n\n## A dead bed resuspends several times more often\n\nCritical bed shear stress: **0.1 Pa** with no biology, **0.5 Pa** with biofilm, tube fauna and eelgrass binding the grains. Same weather, same waves — the only variable is whether the benthos is alive.\n\n| Depth | Live bed | Dead bed | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| 3 m | 2,110 h/yr | 5,352 h/yr | **2.5×** |\n| 5 m | 683 h/yr | 2,897 h/yr | **4.2×** |\n| 10 m | 89 h/yr | 604 h/yr | **6.8×** |\n\nAt 10 m the difference is nearly sevenfold — and the deeper, quieter water is exactly where the fine organic sulphidic mud settles.\n\nThere is a name for what that looks like. Under severe oxygen depletion, white filamentous sulphur bacteria (*Beggiatoa*) spread across the bed in milky sheets, oxidising hydrogen sulphide to sulphate using oxygen taken from the water. Danish calls them **liglagen** — corpse shroud — and they appear in late summer. The mat is the sulphide oxygen sink, visible.\n\nThat matters because resuspending sulphidic sediment is **itself an oxygen sink**, with no nitrogen and no algae in it. At 50 µmol AVS per gram dry sediment, stirring 5 cm consumes about 80 g O₂/m² — the entire oxygen content of a 10 m water column. A storm over a dead bed can strip the water on its own.\n\n### Which produces the loop\n\n1. iltsvind, toxicants or trawling kill the benthos\n2. the erosion threshold falls — the bed becomes loose\n3. storms resuspend more sediment, more often\n4. buried sulphide and metals are re-oxidised and remobilised\n5. resuspended sulphide consumes oxygen; turbidity blocks light\n6. less eelgrass, less benthos — back to step 2\n\n## Seasonality: the bed is stirred hardest in autumn and winter\n\nHours per year above the resuspension threshold at 5 m:\n\n| Month | Live bed | Dead bed | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Jan | 103 | 322 | 3.1× |\n| Feb | 73 | 280 | 3.9× |\n| Mar | 67 | 254 | 3.8× |\n| Apr | 39 | 205 | 5.3× |\n| May | 37 | 188 | 5.1× |\n| Jun | 24 | 172 | 7.1× |\n| Jul | 18 | 153 | 8.7× |\n| Aug | 33 | 195 | 6.0× |\n| Sep | 47 | 230 | 4.9× |\n| Oct | 78 | 301 | 3.9× |\n| Nov | 81 | 300 | 3.7× |\n| Dec | 84 | 296 | 3.5× |\n\nOctober through January runs roughly double July.\n\n*Corrected.* An earlier version of this document said the resuspension season coincides with the overflow season. Over 31 years of rainfall it does not: rain intense enough to overflow a combined sewer peaks in **June to August**, because intensity in Denmark is convective. Resuspension peaks in **October to January**. See [CURRENTS.md](#CURRENTS.md) — the two are separated by a residence time, not simultaneous, and the sequence is deposit in summer, mobilise in autumn.\n\nNote the ratio column: biology protects most in summer (nearly 9× in July) and least in a January gale. Losing the benthos costs you most in the calm season; in a storm the bed moves regardless.\n\n## Which winds do the work\n\n| Sector | Mean fetch | Hours/yr resuspending | Share |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| N | 6.4 km | 12 | 0.4% |\n| NE | 7.9 km | 30 | 1.0% |\n| E | 24.9 km | 422 | 14.6% |\n| SE | 89.4 km | 741 | 25.6% |\n| S | 51.4 km | 421 | 14.5% |\n| SW | 16.0 km | 752 | 25.9% |\n| W | 9.5 km | 468 | 16.1% |\n| NW | 6.1 km | 52 | 1.8% |\n\nSouthwest and southeast each drive about a quarter — but for opposite reasons. Southwesterlies are frequent and short-fetch; southeasterlies are rare and run 89 km. **Southwest does the routine work, southeast does the damage**, and only southeast pushes toward the shore rather than away from it.\n\n## The accumulation term, which iltsvind does not have\n\nFedtemøg requires the biomass to *pile up somewhere*. A bay that produces the same algae and flushes it out does not get fedtemøg. So retention and stranding are part of the causal chain in a way they never are for oxygen depletion.\n\nWind from roughly 70–200° drives surface water, floating mats and their odour onto the western shore and inland:\n\n| Month | Onshore hours | Onshore **and warm** | Onshore **and strong** |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Jan | 212 | 0 | 45 |\n| Feb | 194 | 0 | 28 |\n| Mar | 247 | 2 | 29 |\n| Apr | 291 | 52 | 12 |\n| May | 277 | 156 | 12 |\n| Jun | 216 | 199 | 6 |\n| Jul | 216 | 215 | 3 |\n| Aug | 259 | 256 | 9 |\n| Sep | 254 | 225 | 17 |\n| Oct | 260 | 87 | 35 |\n| Nov | 268 | 5 | 27 |\n| Dec | 205 | 0 | 31 |\n\nOnshore wind is near-constant at 28–40% of hours year round. What changes is what it carries. **Warm-and-onshore peaks July to September** — growth and rotting conditions. **Strong-and-onshore peaks October to January** — the stranding conditions.\n\nWhich gives a sequence rather than a single season: mats grow and begin to putrefy through August and September in warm, weakly-mixed water, and are then driven ashore by the first autumn gales in October and November. That is one phenomenon with two phases, in two different months, and neither is measured.\n\n## What is not here\n\nCurrents. The convergence of wind-driven southward transport against the Baltic outflow is a coherent mechanism for accumulation and would explain why fine sediment and floating material collect in this bay, but it needs current fields that are behind registration. Everything above is wave physics from wind, and says nothing about what arrives from elsewhere.\n\nAlso absent: any measurement. These are computed exceedance frequencies against literature values for critical shear stress, not observations of sediment moving. The ratio between a live and dead bed is robust; the absolute hours depend on a threshold that varies with mud composition.\n########## CURRENTS\n# Where the water goes\n\nGenerated by `scripts/currents.py`. Currents from the Open-Meteo Marine API (CMEMS global physics, hourly, 2022-2026); wind and rain from the ERA5 archive (hourly, 1995-2025). Both free and keyless. Companion to [SEABED.md](#SEABED.md), which computes what the wind lifts off the bed; this asks where it then goes.\n\n## First, what this data cannot do\n\nThe only free current field covering Danish waters is a global model on a roughly 9 km grid. The Danish straits are narrower than that. Before using it for anything, here is the peak speed it produces against published values:\n\n| Point | Model peak | Published peak | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| koege_bugt | 0.50 m/s | 0.4 m/s | 0.8× |\n| oresund_s | 0.89 m/s | 1.5 m/s | 1.7× |\n| drogden | 0.89 m/s | 1.7 m/s | 1.9× |\n| oresund_n | 0.81 m/s | 1.5 m/s | 1.9× |\n| fehmarn | 1.08 m/s | 1.2 m/s | 1.1× |\n| storebaelt | 0.86 m/s | 1.8 m/s | 2.1× |\n\nThe open-water points are about right; the narrow straits come out roughly half the real speed, which is what a 9 km grid does to a 4 km channel. **So nothing below uses an absolute speed.** Everything is a ratio, a sign, or a timing, and each is stated with the reason it survives the calibration error.\n\n## The result: Køge Bugt does not flush\n\nThe metric is the **residual current divided by the mean speed** — how much of the water's motion actually goes somewhere. A factor-of-two error in speed cancels out of a ratio of two speeds, so this number survives the problem above.\n\n| Point | Mean speed | Residual | Residual heading | Flushing time over 20 km |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| koege_bugt | 0.067 m/s | 0.0032 m/s | 142° | **73 days** |\n| storebaelt | 0.180 m/s | 0.0101 m/s | 296° | **23 days** |\n| sydfynske | 0.096 m/s | 0.0265 m/s | 63° | **9 days** |\n| arkona | 0.138 m/s | 0.0351 m/s | 74° | **7 days** |\n| fehmarn | 0.273 m/s | 0.0527 m/s | 342° | **4 days** |\n| oresund_n | 0.220 m/s | 0.0565 m/s | 22° | **4 days** |\n| oresund_s | 0.180 m/s | 0.0638 m/s | 43° | **4 days** |\n| drogden | 0.180 m/s | 0.0638 m/s | 43° | **4 days** |\n| aarhus_bugt | 0.125 m/s | 0.0676 m/s | 36° | **3 days** |\n\n**Køge Bugt takes 73 days to move water 20 km. Aarhus Bugt takes 3.4.** A factor of 22. Køge Bugt has both the lowest mean speed in the set and the smallest residual: the water moves constantly and ends up where it started.\n\n*One caveat, applied honestly.* A low residual can also mean a strong reversing flow with little net — which is what the Great Belt's 23 days is. The Belt has 2.7× Køge Bugt's mean speed; it exchanges water vigorously and just happens to average out. Køge Bugt is slow *and* net-zero. Those are different states and only the second is retention.\n\n### Which inverts the monitoring\n\nAarhus Bugt registers oxygen depletion every year. Køge Bugt is recorded as having none, including in 2023 and 2025. And Aarhus Bugt flushes twenty times faster.\n\nThat is not a contradiction, because the two things are not the same phenomenon. DCE's iltsvind criterion is dissolved oxygen below 4 mg/l in **stratified bottom water** — which requires depth and a sealed layer, and Aarhus Bugt has both. Køge Bugt is shallow and mixes, so it cannot qualify however bad it gets. But retention of surface material, floating mats and fine sediment is a *different* property, and on that one Køge Bugt is the extreme case in this set.\n\nThe national instrument measures the property Køge Bugt does not have, and does not measure the property it has more of than anywhere else here.\n\n**Det Sydfynske Øhav** comes out mid-range at 8.7 days — retentive, but nothing like Køge Bugt. It does register iltsvind. On this evidence the two bays are not the same case, and the shared vortex description is not supported by this model. A 9 km grid cannot resolve an archipelago, so this is weak evidence either way.\n\n## A negative result: the wind index does not work\n\nThe plan was to regress the strait flow on a wind-driven Baltic filling index, and if it held, use the 31-year wind record to extend the 4-year current record. It does not hold.\n\nBest correlation is **r = 0.44 at a 24 hour window**, with sign agreement of only **61%** over 34,968 hours. Correlation decays monotonically at every longer window — 168 h gives 0.17, 336 h gives 0.01.\n\nA 24-hour optimum is a local synoptic wind response, not a basin filling and draining over weeks. Either the multi-week Baltic memory is not the dominant control on the Sound, or this coarse product cannot see it. Reported as a negative result: **the 31-year extension is not available on this data.** Everything about currents here is four years long.\n\n## Does Copenhagen's overflow water go toward Køge Bugt?\n\nCopenhagen discharges into the harbour and the southern Sound. Køge Bugt is south of that, and the mean flow runs north. So the claim is not about averages: it requires that the **specific hours in which the city overflows** are hours in which the water runs south. The rain record and the current record overlap for 35,064 hours, so this is directly testable.\n\nBaseline: the southern Sound runs south **42%** of all hours.\n\n| 6-hour rainfall | Hours | Runs south | vs baseline |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| dry | 23,425 | 42.7% | +0.7 pp |\n| light | 9,099 | 43.0% | +1.0 pp |\n| moderate | 1,695 | 35.0% | -7.0 pp |\n| heavy | 604 | 30.1% | -11.8 pp |\n| overflow-scale | 134 | 23.9% | -18.1 pp |\n\n**During the rain, the water runs north.** The harder it rains, the more strongly — at overflow-scale rainfall, southward transport is 18 points *below* baseline. Which is physically obvious once seen: heavy rain in Copenhagen arrives with cyclonic southwesterlies, and those drive the Sound north.\n\nTaken alone that refutes the transport claim. But an overflow plume does not stop moving when the rain stops:\n\n| Hours after the event | Runs south | vs baseline |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| +0 h | 22.1% | **-19.9 pp** |\n| +6 h | 44.1% | **+2.2 pp** |\n| +12 h | 59.3% | **+17.3 pp** ← |\n| +24 h | 47.6% | **+5.6 pp** |\n| +48 h | 51.0% | **+9.1 pp** |\n| +72 h | 37.2% | **-4.7 pp** |\n\n**Twelve hours after an overflow-scale event, southward transport runs 59% — +17 points above baseline.** That is the post-frontal wind veer: the front passes, the wind swings to the northwest, and the water reverses while the plume is still in it.\n\nSo the mechanism is neither the simple claim nor its refutation. It is a **lag**. The discharge happens under northward flow and the transport reverses roughly half a day later, on a timescale set by the same weather system that caused the discharge.\n\n*Statistical honesty:* this rests on 145 event-hours, and six lags were tested. The 0-hour and 12-hour results are both large and both have the same simple mechanism behind them, which is why they are reported. A longer current record would settle it; four years is what exists.\n\n## A correction to SEABED.md\n\nThat document said the resuspension season coincides with the overflow season. Over 31 years of rainfall that is wrong, and the error is worth keeping visible.\n\n| | Peak months |\n|---|---|\n| Rain intense enough to overflow a combined sewer (≥10 mm in 6 h) | **Jun–Aug**, 4.2–5.1 h/yr; near zero Jan–Apr |\n| Total rainfall | flat, 38–72 mm/month, slight Jun–Aug and Oct maxima |\n| Wave-driven bed resuspension | **Oct–Jan**, roughly double July |\n| Strong onshore wind (stranding) | **Oct–Jan** |\n\nOverflow *events* are driven by intensity, and intensity in Denmark is convective, and convection is summer. The autumn is wetter in total but gentler.\n\nThis does not weaken the case — it sharpens it into a **deposit-then-mobilise sequence**:\n\n1. **June–August:** cloudbursts overflow the combined system. Sewage solids, fat and basin sludge are discharged into a warm, weakly-mixed, retentive bay.\n2. **The bay holds it.** Flushing time is on the order of months, so the material settles locally rather than being exported.\n3. **Through late summer:** it decays in place, in the warmest water of the year, with the oxygen demand and the smell that implies.\n4. **October–January:** the gales arrive. The bed — now looser for having been anoxic — resuspends twice as often as in July, and the same wind that lifts it drives it onto the western shore.\n\nDelivery in summer and arrival on the shore in autumn are not in conflict. They are the two ends of a months-long residence time, and the residence time is the measured part.\n\n## When rain and southward transport coincide\n\n| Month | Overflow-scale hours/yr | ...of those, running south |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Jan | 2.2 | 0.5 |\n| Feb | 0.8 | 0.0 |\n| Mar | 1.0 | 0.0 |\n| Apr | 0.5 | 0.0 |\n| May | 1.0 | 0.0 |\n| Jun | 3.0 | 0.8 |\n| Jul | 8.2 | 1.5 |\n| Aug | 4.0 | 2.8 |\n| Sep | 4.5 | 0.5 |\n| Oct | 6.5 | 1.8 |\n| Nov | 4.0 | 0.0 |\n| Dec | 0.5 | 0.2 |\n\nSmall numbers, and they should be read as small. Wind from the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (1995-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 271,752 hourly records), coastline from OpenStreetMap, everything else computed.\n\n## Why this is computable without a current model\n\nIn a shallow bay the thing that lifts sediment off the bed is orbital motion under waves, and that follows from wind speed, direction, fetch and depth. Currents redistribute what the waves have already lifted — important, and not done here, because it needs data behind registration.\n\nThe chain: wind → fetch by direction (ray-cast to the OSM coastline) → fetch-limited wave height and period (Young & Verhagen 1996, shallow-water form) → bottom orbital velocity (linear wave theory) → bed shear stress (Swart friction factor) → compared against the critical stress for a living bed and a dead one.\n\n## Fetch: Køge Bugt is a southeast-facing funnel\n\n| Wind from | Fetch |\n|---|---:|\n| N | 6.5 km |\n| NE | 7.5 km |\n| E | 31.8 km |\n| SE | **120.0 km** |\n| S | 19.3 km |\n| SW | 17.5 km |\n| W | 9.5 km |\n| NW | 5.8 km |\n\nSoutheast runs to 120 km — the open Baltic approach — against under 20 km in almost every other direction. Southeast is also the **onshore** direction for the western shore. The bay's longest wave fetch and its stranding direction are the same.\n\n## A dead bed resuspends several times more often\n\nCritical bed shear stress: **0.1 Pa** with no biology, **0.5 Pa** with biofilm, tube fauna and eelgrass binding the grains. Same weather, same waves — the only variable is whether the benthos is alive.\n\n| Depth | Live bed | Dead bed | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| 3 m | 2,110 h/yr | 5,352 h/yr | **2.5×** |\n| 5 m | 683 h/yr | 2,897 h/yr | **4.2×** |\n| 10 m | 89 h/yr | 604 h/yr | **6.8×** |\n\nAt 10 m the difference is nearly sevenfold — and the deeper, quieter water is exactly where the fine organic sulphidic mud settles.\n\nThere is a name for what that looks like. Under severe oxygen depletion, white filamentous sulphur bacteria (*Beggiatoa*) spread across the bed in milky sheets, oxidising hydrogen sulphide to sulphate using oxygen taken from the water. Danish calls them **liglagen** — corpse shroud — and they appear in late summer. The mat is the sulphide oxygen sink, visible.\n\nThat matters because resuspending sulphidic sediment is **itself an oxygen sink**, with no nitrogen and no algae in it. At 50 µmol AVS per gram dry sediment, stirring 5 cm consumes about 80 g O₂/m² — the entire oxygen content of a 10 m water column. A storm over a dead bed can strip the water on its own.\n\n### Which produces the loop\n\n1. iltsvind, toxicants or trawling kill the benthos\n2. the erosion threshold falls — the bed becomes loose\n3. storms resuspend more sediment, more often\n4. buried sulphide and metals are re-oxidised and remobilised\n5. resuspended sulphide consumes oxygen; turbidity blocks light\n6. less eelgrass, less benthos — back to step 2\n\n## Seasonality: the bed is stirred hardest in autumn and winter\n\nHours per year above the resuspension threshold at 5 m:\n\n| Month | Live bed | Dead bed | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Jan | 103 | 322 | 3.1× |\n| Feb | 73 | 280 | 3.9× |\n| Mar | 67 | 254 | 3.8× |\n| Apr | 39 | 205 | 5.3× |\n| May | 37 | 188 | 5.1× |\n| Jun | 24 | 172 | 7.1× |\n| Jul | 18 | 153 | 8.7× |\n| Aug | 33 | 195 | 6.0× |\n| Sep | 47 | 230 | 4.9× |\n| Oct | 78 | 301 | 3.9× |\n| Nov | 81 | 300 | 3.7× |\n| Dec | 84 | 296 | 3.5× |\n\nOctober through January runs roughly double July.\n\n*Corrected.* An earlier version of this document said the resuspension season coincides with the overflow season. Over 31 years of rainfall it does not: rain intense enough to overflow a combined sewer peaks in **June to August**, because intensity in Denmark is convective. Resuspension peaks in **October to January**. See [CURRENTS.md](#CURRENTS.md) — the two are separated by a residence time, not simultaneous, and the sequence is deposit in summer, mobilise in autumn.\n\nNote the ratio column: biology protects most in summer (nearly 9× in July) and least in a January gale. Losing the benthos costs you most in the calm season; in a storm the bed moves regardless.\n\n## Which winds do the work\n\n| Sector | Mean fetch | Hours/yr resuspending | Share |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| N | 6.4 km | 12 | 0.4% |\n| NE | 7.9 km | 30 | 1.0% |\n| E | 24.9 km | 422 | 14.6% |\n| SE | 89.4 km | 741 | 25.6% |\n| S | 51.4 km | 421 | 14.5% |\n| SW | 16.0 km | 752 | 25.9% |\n| W | 9.5 km | 468 | 16.1% |\n| NW | 6.1 km | 52 | 1.8% |\n\nSouthwest and southeast each drive about a quarter — but for opposite reasons. Southwesterlies are frequent and short-fetch; southeasterlies are rare and run 89 km. **Southwest does the routine work, southeast does the damage**, and only southeast pushes toward the shore rather than away from it.\n\n## The accumulation term, which iltsvind does not have\n\nFedtemøg requires the biomass to *pile up somewhere*. A bay that produces the same algae and flushes it out does not get fedtemøg. So retention and stranding are part of the causal chain in a way they never are for oxygen depletion.\n\nWind from roughly 70–200° drives surface water, floating mats and their odour onto the western shore and inland:\n\n| Month | Onshore hours | Onshore **and warm** | Onshore **and strong** |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Jan | 212 | 0 | 45 |\n| Feb | 194 | 0 | 28 |\n| Mar | 247 | 2 | 29 |\n| Apr | 291 | 52 | 12 |\n| May | 277 | 156 | 12 |\n| Jun | 216 | 199 | 6 |\n| Jul | 216 | 215 | 3 |\n| Aug | 259 | 256 | 9 |\n| Sep | 254 | 225 | 17 |\n| Oct | 260 | 87 | 35 |\n| Nov | 268 | 5 | 27 |\n| Dec | 205 | 0 | 31 |\n\nOnshore wind is near-constant at 28–40% of hours year round. What changes is what it carries. **Warm-and-onshore peaks July to September** — growth and rotting conditions. **Strong-and-onshore peaks October to January** — the stranding conditions.\n\nWhich gives a sequence rather than a single season: mats grow and begin to putrefy through August and September in warm, weakly-mixed water, and are then driven ashore by the first autumn gales in October and November. That is one phenomenon with two phases, in two different months, and neither is measured.\n\n## What is not here\n\nCurrents. The convergence of wind-driven southward transport against the Baltic outflow is a coherent mechanism for accumulation and would explain why fine sediment and floating material collect in this bay, but it needs current fields that are behind registration. Everything above is wave physics from wind, and says nothing about what arrives from elsewhere.\n\nAlso absent: any measurement. These are computed exceedance frequencies against literature values for critical shear stress, not observations of sediment moving. Currents from the Open-Meteo Marine API (CMEMS global physics, hourly, 2022-2026); wind and rain from the ERA5 archive (hourly, 1995-2025). Both free and keyless. Companion to [SEABED.md](#SEABED.md), which computes what the wind lifts off the bed; this asks where it then goes.\n\n## First, what this data cannot do\n\nThe only free current field covering Danish waters is a global model on a roughly 9 km grid. The Danish straits are narrower than that. Before using it for anything, here is the peak speed it produces against published values:\n\n| Point | Model peak | Published peak | Ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| koege_bugt | 0.50 m/s | 0.4 m/s | 0.8× |\n| oresund_s | 0.89 m/s | 1.5 m/s | 1.7× |\n| drogden | 0.89 m/s | 1.7 m/s | 1.9× |\n| oresund_n | 0.81 m/s | 1.5 m/s | 1.9× |\n| fehmarn | 1.08 m/s | 1.2 m/s | 1.1× |\n| storebaelt | 0.86 m/s | 1.8 m/s | 2.1× |\n\nThe open-water points are about right; the narrow straits come out roughly half the real speed, which is what a 9 km grid does to a 4 km channel. **So nothing below uses an absolute speed.** Everything is a ratio, a sign, or a timing, and each is stated with the reason it survives the calibration error.\n\n## The result: Køge Bugt does not flush\n\nThe metric is the **residual current divided by the mean speed** — how much of the water's motion actually goes somewhere. A factor-of-two error in speed cancels out of a ratio of two speeds, so this number survives the problem above.\n\n| Point | Mean speed | Residual | Residual heading | Flushing time over 20 km |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| koege_bugt | 0.067 m/s | 0.0032 m/s | 142° | **73 days** |\n| storebaelt | 0.180 m/s | 0.0101 m/s | 296° | **23 days** |\n| sydfynske | 0.096 m/s | 0.0265 m/s | 63° | **9 days** |\n| arkona | 0.138 m/s | 0.0351 m/s | 74° | **7 days** |\n| fehmarn | 0.273 m/s | 0.0527 m/s | 342° | **4 days** |\n| oresund_n | 0.220 m/s | 0.0565 m/s | 22° | **4 days** |\n| oresund_s | 0.180 m/s | 0.0638 m/s | 43° | **4 days** |\n| drogden | 0.180 m/s | 0.0638 m/s | 43° | **4 days** |\n| aarhus_bugt | 0.125 m/s | 0.0676 m/s | 36° | **3 days** |\n\n**Køge Bugt takes 73 days to move water 20 km. Aarhus Bugt takes 3.4.** A factor of 22. Køge Bugt has both the lowest mean speed in the set and the smallest residual: the water moves constantly and ends up where it started.\n\n*One caveat, applied honestly.* A low residual can also mean a strong reversing flow with little net — which is what the Great Belt's 23 days is. The Belt has 2.7× Køge Bugt's mean speed; it exchanges water vigorously and just happens to average out. Køge Bugt is slow *and* net-zero. Those are different states and only the second is retention.\n\n### Which inverts the monitoring\n\nAarhus Bugt registers oxygen depletion every year. Køge Bugt is recorded as having none, including in 2023 and 2025. And Aarhus Bugt flushes twenty times faster.\n\nThat is not a contradiction, because the two things are not the same phenomenon. DCE's iltsvind criterion is dissolved oxygen below 4 mg/l in **stratified bottom water** — which requires depth and a sealed layer, and Aarhus Bugt has both. Køge Bugt is shallow and mixes, so it cannot qualify however bad it gets. But retention of surface material, floating mats and fine sediment is a *different* property, and on that one Køge Bugt is the extreme case in this set.\n\nThe national instrument measures the property Køge Bugt does not have, and does not measure the property it has more of than anywhere else here.\n\n**Det Sydfynske Øhav** comes out mid-range at 8.7 days — retentive, but nothing like Køge Bugt. It does register iltsvind. On this evidence the two bays are not the same case, and the shared vortex description is not supported by this model. A 9 km grid cannot resolve an archipelago, so this is weak evidence either way.\n\n## A negative result: the wind index does not work\n\nThe plan was to regress the strait flow on a wind-driven Baltic filling index, and if it held, use the 31-year wind record to extend the 4-year current record. It does not hold.\n\nBest correlation is **r = 0.44 at a 24 hour window**, with sign agreement of only **61%** over 34,968 hours. Correlation decays monotonically at every longer window — 168 h gives 0.17, 336 h gives 0.01.\n\nA 24-hour optimum is a local synoptic wind response, not a basin filling and draining over weeks. Either the multi-week Baltic memory is not the dominant control on the Sound, or this coarse product cannot see it. Reported as a negative result: **the 31-year extension is not available on this data.** Everything about currents here is four years long.\n\n## Does Copenhagen's overflow water go toward Køge Bugt?\n\nCopenhagen discharges into the harbour and the southern Sound. Køge Bugt is south of that, and the mean flow runs north. So the claim is not about averages: it requires that the **specific hours in which the city overflows** are hours in which the water runs south. The rain record and the current record overlap for 35,064 hours, so this is directly testable.\n\nBaseline: the southern Sound runs south **42%** of all hours.\n\n| 6-hour rainfall | Hours | Runs south | vs baseline |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| dry | 23,425 | 42.7% | +0.7 pp |\n| light | 9,099 | 43.0% | +1.0 pp |\n| moderate | 1,695 | 35.0% | -7.0 pp |\n| heavy | 604 | 30.1% | -11.8 pp |\n| overflow-scale | 134 | 23.9% | -18.1 pp |\n\n**During the rain, the water runs north.** The harder it rains, the more strongly — at overflow-scale rainfall, southward transport is 18 points *below* baseline. Det er for bredt, og det er nu rettet til det, dokumenterne faktisk viser — en skærpelse, ikke en tilbagetrækning.\n\n> **For klorofyl og lyssvækkelse findes der en koefficient.** DCE har opstillet statistiske relationer, og indsatsbehovet regnes ud af en hældning: hvor meget indikatoren ændrer sig pr. ændring i N-tilførsel.\n\n> **For iltsvind findes der ingen.** Iltsvindsindikatoren er en *binær udløser*. Hvis én eller flere iltsvindsindikatorer siger, at vandområdet er ramt, sættes indsatsbehovet til en fast reduktion på **25 %** af den nuværende TN-koncentration — uanset hvor slemt iltsvindet er, hvor meget kvælstof der tilføres, eller hvordan området er indrettet. Det er en fagligt begrundet tommelfingerregel, ikke en målt dæmpning. Den kan hverken falsificeres eller kalibreres, fordi der ingen respons-kurve er bag den.\n\n> Det er iltsvind, der bærer den offentlige begrundelse for aftalen. Projektet her bruger det meste af sin plads på at tage byens egne udledninger fra hinanden — regnbetingede overløb, spildevandsplanens huller, hvad Københavns skybrudsplan faktisk dækker. Det er *samme* metode anvendt på kvælstoftallet, og resultatet er ubelejligt for flere end landbruget.\n\n## 1. Hvad de 69,6 % faktisk er en andel af\n\nTallet er landbrugets andel af **den landbaserede, vandbårne post alene** — kvælstof, der når kysten gennem danske vandløb og umålte oplande. Det er to rækker ud af tyve i den opgørelse, projektet har lavet over alle veje, ad hvilke reaktivt kvælstof når danske havområder:\n\n| Række | kt N/år | Grundlag |\n|---|---:|---|\n| Dansk land via målte vandløb | 32 – 38 | delvist målt |\n| Dansk land via umålte oplande | 27 – 33 | modelleret |\n| **Posten, procenten deler** | **59 – 71** | |\n| **69,6 % af den** | **41 – 49** | |\n\nDe **10 af 20 veje har slet intet tal** — heriblandt atmosfærisk afsætning af organisk kvælstof, udsivning af grundvand under havet, og frigivelse fra sedimentet, som efter én undersøgelse leverer størstedelen af det, den årlige primærproduktion kræver. De veje, der *har* et tal, summerer til **167 – 327 kt N/år**.\n\nEn tom række kan kun lægge til. Nævneren har altså et gulv og intet loft, og enhver procent regnet mod den er et **loft, ikke et estimat**:\n\n> Landbruget står for **højst 30 %** af det opgjorte reaktive kvælstof, der når danske havområder. Udfyld én af de tomme rækker, og loftet falder. Det kan ikke stige.\n\nTil sammenligning: **atmosfærisk afsætning direkte på havoverfladen er 45–65 kt N/år** — på størrelse med hele den landbaserede post — og optræder ikke i nogen offentliggjort fordeling.\n\n## 2. Tallet er en restpost, ikke en måling\n\nSådan fremkommer landbrugsandelen: målt-plus-modelleret total, minus modellerede punktkilder, minus modelleret naturligt baggrundsbidrag. Det, der bliver tilbage, kaldes landbrug.\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| Måledækning | 49 % af arealet måles, 51 % modelleres |\n| Målemetode | stikprøver med faste mellemrum, transport beregnet som sum af daglig vandføring gange lineært interpoleret koncentration |\n| Dokumenteret skævhed | i alle tre vandløb i GUDP-undersøgelsen fra 2018 gav stikprøver **altid lavere** transport end højfrekvent måling |\n| Retentionens usikkerhed | ± 16 procentpoint på landsgennemsnittet |\n| Estimatorens opførsel | i tørre år som 1996 og 2005 bliver det beregnede dyrkningsbidrag **negativt** |\n\nEn størrelse, der kan blive negativ, er ikke en måling af en fysisk mængde. Den er residualet af to modeller, og den arver begges fejl med modsat fortegn.\n\n## 3. Tre led mangler mellem tallet og skaden\n\nSætningen, der bruges politisk, er ikke *69,6 % af den landbaserede vandbårne kvælstofpost*. Den er *landbruget står for omkring 70 % af iltsvindet* — eller af fedtemøget. Mellem de to sætninger ligger tre led:\n\n| Led | Koefficient |\n|---|---|\n| Kvælstof → iltsvind | **findes ikke.** Kvælstof er én af mindst seks iltforbrugende processer. Der er ingen potensfaktor: et kilo i februar i en opblandet vandsøjle tæller som et kilo i juli under et springlag |\n| Iltsvind → tab af højere liv | **findes ikke.** Iltsvind er én vej blandt flere — miljøfremmede stoffer, trawl, turbiditet, svovlbrinte. Bundfaunaen prøvetages **1. marts – 31. maj**, så efterårets dødelighed ses aldrig |\n| Tab af højere liv → fedtemøg | **findes ikke.** Fedtemøg overvåges ikke systematisk overhovedet — ikke udbredelse, ikke biomasse, ikke varighed |\n\nHvert led er en reel årsagssammenhæng. Ingen af dem har et tal. **Et produkt af tre ukendte brøker er en ukendt brøk** — og det præsenteres som ét målt tal.\n\n## 4. Prøven, der allerede er taget\n\nDen landbaserede kvælstoftilførsel er faldet fra omkring 100 kt N/år i 1990 til omkring 55 kt — en reduktion på cirka 50 %. Luftbåren kvælstof til danske havområder er faldet tilsvarende. Det er den største miljøindsats i nyere dansk politik, og den er ikke omstridt.\n\nImens:\n\n| År | Iltsvindets udbredelse i september |\n|---|---|\n| 1989 | — |\n| 2000 | — |\n| 2002 | — |\n| 2023 | ~7,500 km² |\n| 2024 | ~11,000 km² |\n| 2025 | ~3,700 km² |\n\n**Halvér tilførslen, og yderpunkterne rykker sig ikke.** 2023 og 2024 lå på niveau med 1989, 2000 og 2002, hvor belastningen var omtrent dobbelt så stor. Og 2025 kom ind på en tredjedel af 2024 — så udsvinget mellem to på hinanden følgende år er større end trenden over femogtredive.\n\nDet er ikke bevis for, at kvælstof er ligegyldigt. Det er bevis for, at **udbredelsen styres af det enkelte års fysik og af havbundens tilstand**, med belastningen som en langsom baggrund. Ingen af de to ting kan en kildeopgørelse overhovedet udtrykke, for ingen af dem er en kilde.\n\n## 5. Det, byen slipper for at få talt med\n\nSamme metode på byens egne udledninger, så det er klart, at kritikken ikke kun peger én vej:\n\n- **Overløbsmængder er modellerede**, ikke målte. PULS registrerer antal overløb og ingen vandføring. Massen beregnes som modelleret årsvolumen gange et fast typetal — og kvalitetskontrolleres ved at tjekke, om koncentrationen ligger tæt på det samme typetal. Usikkerheden på volumen er angivet til 135 % på det laveste videnniveau.\n- **Typetallene for miljøfarlige stoffer** hviler på 6 målestationer for fællessystem og 5 for separat regnvand, anvendt på 19,665 udledningspunkter — i oplande *valgt* til at repræsentere husholdninger og boligområder, og udtrykkeligt afgrænset over for industriområder og stærkt trafikerede veje. Samme rapport finder de højeste medianer for metaller i slam fra bassiner.\n- **Et fællessystemsoverløb leverer lige så meget organisk kulstof direkte, som dets kvælstof kunne nå at producere.** Ved Redfield-forhold svarer 12 mg N/l til 68 mg C/l; vandet bærer selv 68 mg C/l. Kun den ene halvdel tælles, og den tælles til 0,6 % af en national kvælstoftotal.\n- **Fedt indeholder intet kvælstof overhovedet.** Triglycerider er kulstof, brint og ilt. En kvælstofopgørelse kan ikke undervurdere det materiale — den kan slet ikke se det. Og det frigives på en flowtærskel, altså netop i de timer, hvor vandet går uden om renseanlægget.\n\n## 6. Hvad dette **ikke** viser\n\nDette afsnit står her, fordi et argument, der indrømmer hvad det ikke kan vise, er langt sværere at afvise end et, der påstår for meget.\n\n- **Det viser ikke, at landbruget er uden andel.** At gange ukendte brøker giver en ukendt, ikke en lille. Landbruget er sandsynligvis stadig den største enkelte kvælstofkilde, belastningen er reel, og reduktioner har dokumenterede lokale gevinster.\n- **Det viser ikke, at kvælstofpolitikken har fejlet.** *Nødvendig* og *utilstrækkelig* er to forskellige konklusioner, og forløbet siden 1990 er foreneligt med den anden.\n- **Og det er ikke et argument for at gøre ingenting.** Det er et argument for at gøre noget andet — og for at måle det.\n\nDet, det *viser*, er snævrere og stærkere: **grundlaget for et kvantificeret, sektorspecifikt mål er ikke til stede.** Der findes ingen nævner, ingen potensfaktor, og ingen dokumenteret virkning på yderpunkterne efter femogtredive år. Et fejlspecificeret instrument er ikke kun urimeligt over for den regulerede — det er farligt for alle, fordi det bliver ved med at kræve mere af det samme, når det samme ikke virker.\n\n## 7. Hvis begrænsningen er havets evne til at optage, bliver løsningsrummet større\n\nAntag et øjeblik, at skaden ikke er *f(belastning)* men *f(belastning, tilstand)* — at det samme kilo kvælstof gør mere skade i 2025 end i 1990, fordi ålegræsset, filtratorerne og en sammenhængende havbund er væk. Så er der to håndtag, ikke ét, og det andet har hidtil ikke været i spil.\n\n| Virkemiddel | Hvad det gør, som reduktion ikke gør |\n|---|---|\n| **Muslinge- og tangopdræt** | fjerner kvælstof, der **allerede er i vandet**, og høstes i stedet for at rådne. Det eneste virkemiddel, der arbejder på lageret frem for på tilførslen |\n| **Ålegræs og bundintegritet** | genopretter optagelsen og stabiliserer sedimentet, så metaller og svovlbrinte bliver liggende |\n| **Vådområder og efterafgrøder** | de kendte, og de virker — men kun på tilførslen |\n\nDet afgørende ved marin ekstraktion er, at det **er en produktion**. Muslingemel og tang er foder. Og foderet er selve miljøydelsen: kvælstoffet fjernes ved, at biomassen tages op.\n\n## 8. Og dermed et led, der sjældent trækkes\n\nDen bindende omkostning ved at lade et dyr leve længere er foder. Hvis et kvælstofvirkemiddel *producerer* foder og betales som miljøydelse, så kan den samme politik finansiere, at dyr lever længere, i stedet for at besætninger bliver mindre.\n\nDet er ikke en omskrivning. Det er en ændring af, hvad betalingen er knyttet til. I den nuværende ordning falder dyrets værdi sammen med dets død, og jo tidligere jo bedre — tyrekalve, lam, orner. **Et foderflow, der betales for at fjerne kvælstof fra havet, afkobler betalingen fra aflivningen.**\n\nForbeholdene, som skal med, ellers er det reklame:\n\n- Ekstraktivt opdræt opkoncentrerer metaller og organiske miljøfremmede stoffer. Hvor høsten må gå hen, afgøres af analyse, ikke af hensigt — og zink og kobber er ikke det samme som cadmium og kviksølv, som opkoncentreres op gennem fødekæden og som intet levende har et evolutionært beredskab over for.\n- Ekstraktivt opdræt i den nødvendige skala er ikke økonomisk afprøvet. Der er ikke sket en effektivitetsrevolution endnu — men der er heller ikke gjort noget alvorligt forsøg.\n- Og intet af dette fritager nogen. Det udvider listen over, hvad der kan gøres.\n\n## 9. Hvad man konkret kan forlange\n\nIkke *drop kravet*. Det er en tabt sag og en dårlig sag. I stedet fire ting, som alle er billige, og som ingen kan afvise uden at forklare hvorfor:\n\n| Krav | Hvorfor det ikke kan afvises |\n|---|---|\n| **Offentliggør regressionen.** Iltsvindets årlige udbredelse mod flow-normaliseret belastning, vindarbejde i lagdelingssæsonen og bundvandstemperatur | alle tre serier er allerede offentliggjort af DCE. Det kræver ingen nye data, ingen nye målinger og ingen bevilling |\n| **Udfyld nævneren.** Mindst de to tomme rækker, der kan måles med standardmetoder — udsivning af grundvand under havet med radon- og radiumsporing, og intern frigivelse fra sedimentet med bundkamre | begge er rutine i udlandet. Uden en nævner er der ingen procent |\n| **Mål overløbene i hændelser.** Flowproportional prøvetagning på de største bygværker, over hændelser af forskellig størrelse | det er videnniveau 5 i Miljøstyrelsens egen skala, med 30 % usikkerhed mod 135 %. Metoden er defineret. Næsten ingen bruger den |\n| **Finansiér marin ekstraktion som virkemiddel**, med krav om analyse af høsten | det er det eneste virkemiddel, der fjerner kvælstof, som allerede er i vandet |\n\nDe tre første er krav om *måling*. Det er den stærkeste position, man kan indtage over for et tal, man mener er forkert: forlang ikke, at det ændres — forlang, at det bliver efterprøvet.\n\n---\n\n## In English\n\nThis page argues, in Danish and to a Danish agricultural audience, that the evidential chain from the published 69.6% figure to a quantified sector-specific reduction target has three missing links: there is no closed denominator (10 of 20 enumerated nitrogen pathways carry no number), no coefficient anywhere between nitrogen and any outcome, and no detectable movement in the extremes after a 35-year halving of the load. It states explicitly that this does not exonerate agriculture, that multiplying unknown fractions yields an unknown rather than a small one, and that it is not an argument for inaction. It applies the same scrutiny to urban discharge, where the numbers are worse. And it ends with four demands, three of which are demands for measurement rather than for a different answer.\n\nThe full audit is in [NITROGEN.md](#NITROGEN.md) and [CAUSATION.md](#CAUSATION.md); the argument about what to build instead is in [PROGRAMME.md](#PROGRAMME.md).\n\n*Denne side er skrevet af en ikke-modersmålstalende og bør læses igennem af en dansker, før den citeres.*","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"ed3c2d24-850b-4d01-9632-597ddcdc1113","timestamp":"2026-09-08T02:05:49.274Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Til landbruget: grundlaget for kravet\n\n> ## Om denne sides påstand om koefficienter\n\n> En tidligere version af denne side sagde, at der *ikke findes nogen koefficient mellem kvælstof og nogen økologisk effekt*. Det er for bredt, og det er nu rettet til det, dokumenterne faktisk viser — en skærpelse, ikke en tilbagetrækning.\n\n> **For klorofyl og lyssvækkelse findes der en koefficient.** DCE har opstillet statistiske relationer, og indsatsbehovet regnes ud af en hældning: hvor meget indikatoren ændrer sig pr. ændring i N-tilførsel.\n\n> **For iltsvind findes der ingen.** Iltsvindsindikatoren er en *binær udløser*. Hvis begrænsningen er havets evne til at optage, bliver løsningsrummet større\n\nAntag et øjeblik, at skaden ikke er *f(belastning)* men *f(belastning, tilstand)* — at det samme kilo kvælstof gør mere skade i 2025 end i 1990, fordi ålegræsset, filtratorerne og en sammenhængende havbund er væk. Det eneste virkemiddel, der arbejder på lageret frem for på tilførslen |\n| **Ålegræs og bundintegritet** | genopretter optagelsen og stabiliserer sedimentet, så metaller og svovlbrinte bliver liggende |\n| **Vådområder og efterafgrøder** | de kendte, og de virker — men kun på tilførslen |\n\nDet afgørende ved marin ekstraktion er, at det **er en produktion**. Muslingemel og tang er foder. Og foderet er selve miljøydelsen: kvælstoffet fjernes ved, at biomassen tages op.\n\n## 8. Og dermed et led, der sjældent trækkes\n\nDen bindende omkostning ved at lade et dyr leve længere er foder. Hvis et kvælstofvirkemiddel *producerer* foder og betales som miljøydelse, så kan den samme politik finansiere, at dyr lever længere, i stedet for at besætninger bliver mindre.\n\nDet er ikke en omskrivning. Det er en ændring af, hvad betalingen er knyttet til. I den nuværende ordning falder dyrets værdi sammen med dets død, og jo tidligere jo bedre — tyrekalve, lam, orner. **Et foderflow, der betales for at fjerne kvælstof fra havet, afkobler betalingen fra aflivningen.**\n\nForbeholdene, som skal med, ellers er det reklame:\n\n- Ekstraktivt opdræt opkoncentrerer metaller og organiske miljøfremmede stoffer. Hvor høsten må gå hen, afgøres af analyse, ikke af hensigt — og zink og kobber er ikke det samme som cadmium og kviksølv, som opkoncentreres op gennem fødekæden og som intet levende har et evolutionært beredskab over for.\n- Ekstraktivt opdræt i den nødvendige skala er ikke økonomisk afprøvet. Der er ikke sket en effektivitetsrevolution endnu — men der er heller ikke gjort noget alvorligt forsøg.\n- Og intet af dette fritager nogen. Det udvider listen over, hvad der kan gøres.\n\n## 9. Hvad man konkret kan forlange\n\nIkke *drop kravet*. Det er en tabt sag og en dårlig sag. I stedet fire ting, som alle er billige, og som ingen kan afvise uden at forklare hvorfor:\n\n| Krav | Hvorfor det ikke kan afvises |\n|---|---|\n| **Offentliggør regressionen.** Iltsvindets årlige udbredelse mod flow-normaliseret belastning, vindarbejde i lagdelingssæsonen og bundvandstemperatur | alle tre serier er allerede offentliggjort af DCE. Det kræver ingen nye data, ingen nye målinger og ingen bevilling |\n| **Udfyld nævneren.** Mindst de to tomme rækker, der kan måles med standardmetoder — udsivning af grundvand under havet med radon- og radiumsporing, og intern frigivelse fra sedimentet med bundkamre | begge er rutine i udlandet. Uden en nævner er der ingen procent |\n| **Mål overløbene i hændelser.** Flowproportional prøvetagning på de største bygværker, over hændelser af forskellig størrelse | det er videnniveau 5 i Miljøstyrelsens egen skala, med 30 % usikkerhed mod 135 %. Metoden er defineret. Næsten ingen bruger den |\n| **Finansiér marin ekstraktion som virkemiddel**, med krav om analyse af høsten | det er det eneste virkemiddel, der fjerner kvælstof, som allerede er i vandet |\n\nDe tre første er krav om *måling*. Det er den stærkeste position, man kan indtage over for et tal, man mener er forkert: forlang ikke, at det ændres — forlang, at det bliver efterprøvet.\n\n---\n\n## In English\n\nThis page argues, in Danish and to a Danish agricultural audience, that the evidential chain from the published 69.6% figure to a quantified sector-specific reduction target has three missing links: there is no closed denominator (10 of 20 enumerated nitrogen pathways carry no number), no coefficient anywhere between nitrogen and any outcome, and no detectable movement in the extremes after a 35-year halving of the load. It states explicitly that this does not exonerate agriculture, that multiplying unknown fractions yields an unknown rather than a small one, and that it is not an argument for inaction. It applies the same scrutiny to urban discharge, where the numbers are worse. And it ends with four demands, three of which are demands for measurement rather than for a different answer.\n\nThe full audit is in [NITROGEN.md](#NITROGEN.md) and [CAUSATION.md](#CAUSATION.md); the argument about what to build instead is in [PROGRAMME.md](#PROGRAMME.md).\n\n*Denne side er skrevet af en ikke-modersmålstalende og bør læses igennem af en dansker, før den citeres.*","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4a19282c-d841-44d0-9389-588d806be63d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/user/projects/copenhagen-waterways","sessionId":"a357d1ab-60f3-479a-9941-a683a24b19ae","version":"2.1.263","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"harmonic-churning-simon"}

Havområdet omfattet af havstrate-\ngidirektivet svarer til EEZ (eksklusiv økonomisk zone), som strækker sig maksimalt 200 sømil ud fra den\ndanske kyst, men i praksis hovedsageligt udgøres af midterlinjen til Danmarks nabolande.\n2.3.1      Overvågning i henhold til vandrammedirektivet samt\n           iltsvindsprogram\nOvervågningen relateret til opnåelse af god økologisk tilstand i henhold til vandrammedirekti-\nvet omfatter biologiske kvalitetselementer – fytoplankton, makroalger, ålegræs, andre blom-\nsterplanter og bundfauna – samt supplerende fysisk-kemiske (næringssalte og ilt) og hydro-\nmorfologiske (sedimentforhold) kvalitetselementer.\nDer er udpeget 109 vandområder inden for 1-sømilsgrænsen, hvor der skal opnås god økolo-\ngisk og kemisk tilstand, og 14 vandområder inden for 12-sømilsgrænsen, hvor der skal opnås\ngod kemisk tilstand. God kemisk tilstand omfatter en række miljøfarlige forurenende stoffer,\nder som nævnt ovenfor overvåges i regi af delprogram for miljøfarlige forurenende stoffer og\nfor punktkilder (kapitel 6).\nMed den samlede kontrol- og operationelle overvågning beskrevet nedenfor vil der blive gen-\nnemført overvågning af vandrammedirektivets kvalitetselementer i alle 109 vandområder inden\nfor 1-sømilsgrænsen (med de nedenfor nævnte undtagelser). Dette er en opjustering i forhold\ntil NOVANA 2017-21, hvor der ikke forekom overvågning af fytoplankton (her klorofyl) og\nbundfaunakvalitetselementet i alle vandområder. områder\n       Kontrolovervågning\n       Denne overvågning gennemføres med enkelte undtagelser hvert år og er fordelt geografisk på\n       både fjordområder, kystvande og mere åbne havområder. Vurderingen af langtidsændringer\n       sikres ved en videreførelse af stationer med lange tidsserier. Kontrolovervågning af den økolo-\n       giske tilstand sker årligt for en række centrale biologiske og fysisk-kemiske parametre – fyto-\n       plankton (klorofyl, algevækst og artssammensætning), ålegræs og andre blomsterplanter, ma-\n       kroalger, blødbundsfauna, hydrografiske profilmålinger (salt, temperatur, ilt mv.), næringsstof-\n       fer i vand og sediment. Hvis kontrolovervågningen af de af de nævnte parametre, der indgår i\n       tilstandsvurderinger, er placeret i områder, der er i risiko for ikke at opfylde målet om god mil-\n       jøtilstand, anvendes den på lige fod med den operationelle overvågning i tilstandsvurderinger.\n       Et særligt nationalt behov er desuden overvågning af iltsvind, som foretages hvert år i som-\n       mer- og efterårsmånederne på et stort antal stationer ud over dem, som er omfattet af over-\n       vågningen af vandkemi herunder iltforhold.\n20 Miljøstyrelsen / NOVANA 2023-27\n\fDerudover er der en række aktiviteter, som understøtter vurderingerne af den generelle miljø-\ntilstand samt langtidsændringer i henhold til vandrammedirektivet. Eksempelvis omfatter over-\nvågningen i mere åbne områder i Kattegat, Bælthavet og Østersøen samt overvågningen i\nNordsøen bl.a. indsamling af prøver til bestemmelse af næringssalte i vinterperioden (februar-\nmarts). Overvågningen foretages bl.a. for at kunne vurdere ophavet til, og næringsstofniveau-\nerne i, vandmasserne i Kattegat og Bælthavet i det tidlige forår. Filtrerende bunddyr undersø-\nges i Ringkøbing Fjord, bl.a. fordi sandmuslingerne dér repræsenterer et unikt eksempel på, at\nen ændret fysisk påvirkning – i dette tilfælde en ændret slusepraksis, der har påvirket salthol-\ndigheden – har ændret økosystemets struktur og funktion i form af sammensætningen af\nbundfauna og derved algemængden i vandet.\nI kontrolovervågningen indgår desuden undersøgelser af havbundens organiske stofindhold\nog næringsstofpuljer, som udover at afspejle langtidsændringer i næringsstofbelastning og/el-\nler -aflastning også udnyttes til at forbedre de marine økosystemmodeller og kvantificere hav-\nbundens indhold af kulstof. Da disse puljer ændrer sig relativt langsomt, gennemføres denne\novervågning ikke årligt.\nOperationel overvågning\nDen operationelle overvågning omfatter de kvalitetselementer, der indgår i vandrammedirekti-\nvet. Overvågningen omfatter således fytoplankton (målt som klorofyl), ålegræs og andre blom-\nsterplanter samt makroalger, blødbundsfauna og endelig fysisk-kemiske parametre som næ-\nringsstoffer og hydrografiske profilmålinger (saltholdighed, temperatur, ilt, lys mv.).
